summary: A regional folklore article about the Witch of the Willow Woods, a legend centered on the town of Eldersham that began in September 2023. It recounts the first sighting, the disappearance of farmer Jonathan Greyleaf, the witch's backstory as the healer Arabella Sowthistle, and later encounters. It notes how the legend inspired the Willow Woodlands Preserve and ends with a call for readers to share their own stories.
one_line: Article on the Eldersham legend of the Witch of the Willow Woods, from first sighting in 2023 to conservation efforts and a call for reader stories.
key_facts: The legend of the Witch of the Willow Woods is said to have been passed down since the autumn of September 2023, centered on the Willow Woods near the town of Eldersham.
On September 13, 2023, Eliza Maplewood reported seeing a cloaked elderly woman with eyes that glinted like stars at the edge of the woods, but no villager could confirm the sighting.
On October 22, 2023, farmer Jonathan Greyleaf, known for disdaining superstition, entered the woods to debunk the myths and never came out; only a tattered scarf on a weeping willow branch was found.
The witch was reportedly once a healer named Arabella Sowthistle, who was blamed for a sickness that swept through Eldersham after the harsh winter of 2023.
Arabella Sowthistle retreated into the Willow Woods and vowed to protect nature; her spirit is said to be bound to the willows, cursing those who harm the forest.
On November 11, 2023, birdwatcher Luna Northwind said she saw a willow tree bend its branches to shield a nest during a storm.
In December 2023, hunter Gerald Oakthorn said an unseen force snatched his arrow from the air just before it would have hit a doe.
On January 15, 2024, local artist Holly Green reported a profound peace while painting en plein air beneath the willows, inspiring belief that the witch is also a guardian.
On March 5, 2024, environmentalist Felix Brambles established the Willow Woodlands Preserve to uphold the spirit's alleged wishes.
The willows are rumored to ward off those with malevolent hearts while leaving untouched those who truly love the earth.
The reporter invites readers to share stories using the hashtag #WillowWoodsWitch or by sending them to the Eldersham Gazette.
